q: How far is Martin Brod from Bihać?
a: Martin Brod is about 50 km from Bihać, roughly an hour's drive. The route heads south via Ripač, Orašac and Kulen Vakuf, and beyond Kulen Vakuf there is a short gravel section. Martin Brod is part of the City of Bihać and of Una National Park.

q: How do I get from Bihać to Martin Brod?
a: From Bihać drive south along the Una via Ripač and Lohovo to Orašac, then on to Kulen Vakuf. From Kulen Vakuf it is roughly another 15 minutes to Martin Brod, and on this stretch a short gravel section follows where the tarmac ends. Follow the brown signs for Una National Park.

q: What is there to see in Martin Brod?
a: Martin Brod is home to the Milančev buk waterfalls, the largest group of waterfalls in Una National Park, and the confluence of the Unac and the Una. There is also Rmanj Monastery, old watermills, a bučnica (water-powered wool washer) more than 300 years old, and the Martina staza and Put pod gredu walking trails. You buy a ticket for the waterfalls at entrance number 5.

q: What is Milančev buk?
a: Milančev buk is a series of waterfalls and cascades on the Una in Martin Brod, about 800 metres long with a total drop of around 54 metres. According to Una National Park, it is the largest and longest group of waterfalls in the park. It stretches alongside the village all the way to the mouth of the Unac.

q: How high is Milančev buk waterfall?
a: Milančev buk is not a single tall waterfall but a series of falls and cascades, with a total drop of about 54 metres over a length of around 800 metres. That is why some sources describe it as a waterfall of around 50 metres. It looks its best in spring, when the water is high.

q: Is there an entrance fee for Milančev buk?
a: Yes, Milančev buk is in the Martin Brod zone of Una National Park, and you buy a ticket at entrance number 5. The ticket covers the Milančev buk and Jalački buk waterfalls, and there is also a combined ticket with Štrbački buk. Check current prices on the official website, npuna.com.

q: Where is Rmanj Monastery?
a: Rmanj Monastery is near Martin Brod, where the Unac flows into the Una, and you can see it as you enter the village. It is an Orthodox monastery and an important spiritual centre for the border region of Bosnia, Lika and Dalmatia. When visiting, respect the dress code and the rules of conduct for religious sites.

q: How old is Rmanj Monastery?
a: Rmanj Monastery dates from the Middle Ages, and most sources place it in the 15th century. Local tradition links its founding to Katarina Branković and her son Herman, after whom, according to legend, it was named. Monks returned in 1998, and a new monastery residence was consecrated in 2006.

q: Where is Kulen Vakuf and how far is it from Bihać?
a: Kulen Vakuf is a small town on the Una south of Bihać, inside Una National Park, about 45 km from Bihać. It is the largest settlement in the park and lies on the road to Martin Brod. From Bihać the drive takes about 45 minutes. Above the town stands the medieval Ostrovica fortress.

q: What is there to see in Kulen Vakuf?
a: In Kulen Vakuf it is worth seeing the Ottoman-era mosque in the centre, the old bazaar quarter (čaršija) and the bridges over the Una. Above the town is the old Ostrovica fortress with views over the Una valley, and across the river are the ruins of the Havala fortress. Kulen Vakuf is also a good place to stop for lunch, with trout from the Una.

q: What is Ostrovica fortress?
a: Ostrovica is a medieval fortress on a wooded ridge above Kulen Vakuf, on the left bank of the Una. It is first mentioned in 1407, was taken by the Ottomans in 1523 and abandoned in 1878. It is a national monument of Bosnia and Herzegovina and has been partly restored. From the top there is a view over Kulen Vakuf and the Una valley.

q: How do I get to Ostrovica fortress?
a: Ostrovica is reached from Kulen Vakuf, with a walk uphill to the fortress itself. The climb is short but steep, so you will need shoes with good grip and, in summer, water. The ruins are partly collapsed, so take care on the walls. Allow roughly one to two hours for the climb and visit, including a rest at the top.

q: What is Havala fortress?
a: Havala is an Ottoman fortress from the mid-17th century on the right bank of the Una, opposite Ostrovica and Kulen Vakuf. Its job was to guard the bridge over the Una and the road towards Lika and Dalmatia. Today only ruins remain, and it sees fewer visitors than Ostrovica.

q: Where is Klisa near Bihać?
a: Klisa is a small village in the City of Bihać area, on the road between Orašac and Kulen Vakuf, in the Una valley. According to the 2013 census it had about 180 inhabitants. You pass through Klisa when driving from Orašac towards Kulen Vakuf and Martin Brod.

q: Is there anything to see in Klisa?
a: Klisa is a quiet village without major sights, but it lies on a lovely stretch of road along the Una between Orašac and Kulen Vakuf. The drive through this part of the valley offers views of the river and the surrounding hills. Most visitors simply pass through Klisa on their way to Ostrovica and Martin Brod.

q: How can I see Štrbački buk, Kulen Vakuf and Martin Brod in one day?
a: Leave Bihać in the morning and drive via Orašac to Štrbački buk; after your visit, return to the main road and continue towards Kulen Vakuf. Stop there at Ostrovica and for lunch, then in the afternoon see Milančev buk and Rmanj Monastery in Martin Brod. In the evening you drive back to Bihać in about an hour.

q: How far is it from Štrbački buk to Martin Brod?
a: From Štrbački buk you drive back to Orašac and continue via Kulen Vakuf. Because of the gravel access road to the waterfall and the narrow stretch towards Martin Brod, the drive takes about 45 minutes. Both places are easy to visit on the same day, and you can stop at Ostrovica in Kulen Vakuf on the way.

q: How far is it from Kulen Vakuf to Martin Brod?
a: The drive from Kulen Vakuf to Martin Brod takes about 15 minutes. As you leave Kulen Vakuf, a short gravel section follows where the tarmac ends, and then it is tarmac again. The road is fine for ordinary cars. It runs along the Una, so you can stop to take photos of the river on the way.

q: What are the roads like to Martin Brod and Kulen Vakuf?
a: The road from Bihać via Orašac to Kulen Vakuf is tarmac, but it is narrow and winding, so the drive takes longer than the distance suggests. Towards Martin Brod there is a short gravel section, and the access road to Štrbački buk is partly gravel. In summer expect farm vehicles and cyclists on the road.

q: Do I need to cross a border on the way to Martin Brod?
a: No, the route from Bihać via Orašac and Kulen Vakuf to Martin Brod stays in Bosnia and Herzegovina the whole way. Sat-navs sometimes suggest a route through Croatia, but then you cross the border twice. The simplest option is to follow the signs for Kulen Vakuf and Una National Park.

q: Is Martin Brod a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
a: The tufa waterfalls at Martin Brod were added to Bosnia and Herzegovina's Tentative List for World Heritage in 2019. That means they are a candidate but not on UNESCO's final list. Una National Park is pushing for a nomination together with Štrbački buk. Being on the Tentative List helps with protection but changes nothing for visitors.

q: Can you swim in Martin Brod?
a: Inside the national park you may only swim in the Una at designated spots and never within 50 metres of waterfalls, which includes Milančev buk. Swimming in the Unac and the park's other rivers is not allowed. Ask at entrance number 5 exactly where swimming is permitted.

q: Is there a picnic area in Martin Brod?
a: Yes, the Lučica picnic area by entrance number 5 has covered tables and benches. It also has fixed barbecues, one of the few places in the park where fires are allowed. Lučica is also where the Una Regatta opens at the end of July.

q: What is the bučnica in Martin Brod?
a: A bučnica is an old wooden water-powered device in which the force of the Una washes and softens woollen blankets, which is why it is called a natural washing machine. The one in Martin Brod is about 200 metres from the waterfall and is thought to be more than 300 years old. Old watermills can be seen next to it.

q: Where does the name Martin Brod come from?
a: According to local legend, the name Martin Brod comes from the story of two young lovers whose ill-fated romance gave the place its name. The Martina staza walking trail is a reminder of this legend. The village has a long history and is mentioned in records as early as the 14th and 15th centuries.

q: Are there restaurants in Martin Brod and Kulen Vakuf?
a: Martin Brod and Kulen Vakuf have local restaurants and inns, mostly serving fish from the Una, especially trout. What is open and when depends on the season, and outside summer some places are closed. Bring water and something to eat, and if you want to be sure of dinner, head back to Bihać.

q: How much time do you need for Martin Brod?
a: Two to three hours is enough for a walk along Milančev buk, a visit to Rmanj Monastery and a look around the village. Including the drive from Bihać and back, allow half a day or more. Combined with Štrbački buk and Kulen Vakuf, it makes a full-day trip.

q: Is Martin Brod suitable for children?
a: Yes, Martin Brod is family-friendly, with paths along the waterfalls, the Lučica picnic area and places to rest. Keep children close by the water, as the tufa rocks and paths are slippery. Children under 7 get into Una National Park for free.

q: Can you go rafting in Martin Brod?
a: Yes, boating, kayaking and rafting are allowed on the Martin Brod – Kulen Vakuf stretch with a special park ticket and through licensed operators. This is a different stretch from the rafting section at Grmuša near Bihać. For our guests we organise rafting at Grmuša with Una Olympic Rafting.

q: Can I take my dog to Martin Brod?
a: Dogs are allowed in Una National Park only on a lead, but under park rules they are not permitted on the paths in Martin Brod or in religious buildings. So you can go into the village and the picnic area with your dog, but not onto the waterfall paths. Check the rules on npuna.com before your visit.

q: What is the best day-trip route through Una National Park?
a: The classic route runs from Bihać via Orašac to Štrbački buk, then through Klisa to Kulen Vakuf and Ostrovica, and finally to Martin Brod. In total that is about 120 km of driving in a loop, plus a few hours of sightseeing. Set off early so you can see everything without rushing and be back before dark.

q: Which is better, Martin Brod or Štrbački buk?
a: Štrbački buk is a single tall, powerful waterfall of 24.5 metres, while Martin Brod is a series of waterfalls and cascades with views of the village, mills and monastery. Štrbački buk is closer and better known; Martin Brod is quieter and more varied. If you have a full day, visit both.

q: Is Martin Brod worth visiting in winter?
a: Martin Brod has a quiet, misty beauty in winter, with hardly any visitors. In winter the roads are slower because of snow and ice, and some restaurants are closed. Check road conditions and the announcements on npuna.com before setting off. As at Štrbački buk, the waterfalls are often wrapped in mist in winter, with ice along the edges.

q: Where should I stay for a trip to Martin Brod and Kulen Vakuf?
a: The most practical places to stay are Bihać or Lohovo, which is on the way to Orašac and Kulen Vakuf. On apartmanibihac.com a whole apartment, up to 100 m², costs from €25, or 50 KM, per night, roughly the price of a single room in Bihać. You can also send an enquiry via WhatsApp/Viber on +387 61 591 320.

q: What is the history of Kulen Vakuf?
a: For centuries Kulen Vakuf was an important crossroads on the Una, and a Roman road between Dalmatia and Pannonia once ran through it. In Ottoman times the town grew up around a mosque and a large bridge, and was called Džisr-i-kebir, meaning 'Great Bridge'. It got its present name in the 19th century.

q: Is there fishing in Kulen Vakuf?
a: Yes, near Kulen Vakuf there is a fly-fishing section on the Una about 1.5 km long, where all fish must be released. You need a valid permit to fish in Una National Park. Check the types of permit and the rules on npuna.com. On other stretches of the Una in the park, the rules limit the number and size of fish you can keep.

q: What is Pogledalo near Martin Brod?
a: Pogledalo is a viewpoint near Martin Brod overlooking the Una valley and the surrounding area. You reach it on foot, so bring comfortable shoes. Ask at the park's information point in Martin Brod for the exact route. Local guides and hosts in the village will gladly show you the way.

q: Can you drive from Martin Brod to Drvar?
a: Yes, from Martin Brod the road continues along the Unac towards Drvar, the direction the Unac flows from. This stretch has little traffic and is narrow in places. If you are planning a loop, check road conditions before setting off. From Drvar you can return to Bihać via Bosanski Petrovac.

q: What should I bring on a trip to Martin Brod and Kulen Vakuf?
a: Bring cash in convertible marks for tickets, comfortable shoes for slippery paths and the climb to Ostrovica, and water and something to eat. In summer you will need a hat and sun cream, and for a visit to Rmanj Monastery suitable clothing that covers shoulders and knees. Fill up with fuel in Bihać, as there are not many petrol stations along the way.

q: Is there a railway in Martin Brod?
a: The old Una Railway (Unska pruga) runs through Martin Brod, and the village has a station and a well-known railway bridge. The bridge makes a good photo, especially from the banks of the Una. Regular passenger services on the line are limited, so plan to travel to Martin Brod by car.
